tagline: Over a ridge that only two rivers ever got through.
intro: Out of Whitesburg, in the valley of the North Fork of the Kentucky River, US 119 turns southwest and goes up Pine Mountain. The ridge runs about 125 miles across three states and has long stood in the way of traffic. Only the Cumberland River at Pineville and the Clear Fork near Jellico pass all the way through it.

Here the mountain goes unofficially by the name of Whitesburg Mountain, and the road has been widened in places on the climb to make it safer for trucks. It goes over the 2,800-foot mountain, crosses the Little Shepherd Trail and comes down to Oven Fork on the Cumberland, a little over eight miles in all.

moments.title: Whitesburg
moments.text: The county seat, founded in 1842 and first called Summit City, was renamed for John D. White, the legislator who had brought in the bill that created Letcher County.

moments.title: Oven Fork
moments.text: The settlement on the Cumberland may have its name from a brick oven that fired bricks for the chimneys hereabouts, or from Germans who baked their bread in the open.

moments.title: Bad Branch Falls State Nature Preserve
moments.text: In a narrow gorge cut into the face of Pine Mountain near Whitesburg, a 1.8-mile loop through hemlock forest leads to a 60-foot waterfall coming over sandstone cliffs.
